content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":3,"description_fidelity":5,"readability_1x":4,"pixel_craft":4,"palette_discipline":3,"appeal":4},"score":39,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The roughly 30-pixel-wide silhouette exceeds the intended 16-20 px footprint and feels like a horizontal ship rather than a compact squid mine.","The three long, parallel appendages on the right read as mechanical rails or exhaust fins, not gathered/thrusting tentacles.","At 1x, the white face, two red blocks, and black interior merge into a busy cluster; the body and eyes are not immediately separable.","The upper body is a large rectangular blue mass with a flat black roof, lacking the economical rounded silhouette typical of MM2/MM3 enemies.","Contour weight is inconsistent: heavy black masses surround the face and appendage roots while portions of the blue extremities have weak or interrupted outlines.","Blue, red, white, and black occupy the same central tile regions, exceeding normal NES sprite-palette discipline unless built from conspicuous overlapping sprites.","The permanently prominent red eyes weaken the described warning-flash behavior and compete with the large red body stripe.","The blunt, uneven appendage ends and isolated far-right black cap make the sprite feel assembled from bars rather than clean pixel clusters."],"fixes":["Compress the sprite to about 18x18 px: use an 11-12 px rounded mantle and keep all tentacles within another 5-7 px.","Replace the horizontal blue rails with three short, tapered tentacles that bend inward in one frame and flare backward in a thrust frame.","Rebuild the mantle with a consistent one-pixel black contour and stepped 1-2-2-1 curves; remove the long flat top and heavy interior black blocks.","Simplify the face to a clean white visor or two small eye windows, with one-pixel pupils and at least one pixel of separation from surrounding outlines.","Use black, blue, and white for the normal frame; swap the eye pixels to red in a dedicated warning frame rather than carrying the large red stripe.","If red and white must appear together, confine the red warning eyes to a small overlapping hardware sprite with deliberate 8x8 placement.","Shorten and align the appendage endpoints, remove the far-right black nub, and give each limb a clear one-pixel outlined tip.","Make the lower contour slightly bulbous or pointed and place the tentacles beneath/rearward so the silhouette reads as a floating robotic squid rather than a side-view vehicle."]}
